This powerful tribe made frequent incursions against the Hebrews. There was almost perpetual war between them.

Two resting-places, a little village in the tribe of Issachar, to the north of Jezreel and south of Mount Gilboa (Josh. 19:18), where the Philistines encamped when they came against Saul (1 Sam. 28:4), and where Elisha was hospitably entertained by a rich woman of the place. Boiling spring, a mountain range, now Jebel Fukua', memorable as the scene of Saul's disastrous defeat by the Philistines. Here also his three sons were slain, and he himself died by his own hand (1 Sam. 28:4; 31:1-8; 2 Sam. 1:6-21; 21:12; 1 Chr. 10:1, 8).
ch.s: This chapter covers: Achish puts confidence in David, Saul's fear (vv. 1–6); Saul consults a witch at Endor (vv. 7–19); Saul's terror (vv. 20–25). People named: Saul, Samuel, David, Achish, Ramah, Urim. Places: Philistines, Shunem, Gilboa, Amalek.
ch.mh: David could not refuse Achish without danger.
q: Read verses 1–6 (Achish puts confidence in David, Saul's fear). What is happening, and what stands out to you most?
In verses 7–19 (Saul consults a witch at Endor), what do you learn about war and conflict?
Verse 6 is one of the most cross-referenced verses in this chapter. Read it alongside Numbers 12:6. How do the two passages shed light on each other?
What does Saul’s part in this chapter teach you — as an example to follow or a warning to heed?
Where do you see the theme of the holy spirit in this chapter, and how does it connect to the rest of 1 Samuel?
What is one specific way you can put this chapter into practice this week?
ch.a: Set aside a specific time this week to pray through this chapter's key verse.

Angry, perhaps only a general title of royalty applicable to the Philistine kings. (1.) The king with whom David sought refuge when he fled from Saul (1 Sam. 21:10-15). He is called Abimelech in the superscription of Ps. 34.

ch.mh: David waited with a secret hope that the Lord would help him out of his difficulty.

A town in the Negeb, or south country of Judah (Josh. 15:31), in the possession of the Philistines when David fled to Gath from Ziph with all his followers. Achish, the king, assigned him Ziklag as his place of residence.

Cold, a ravine or brook in the extreme south-west of Judah, where 200 of David's men stayed behind because they were faint, while the other 400 pursued the Amalekites (1 Sam. 30:9, 10, 21). Probably the Wadyes Sheriah, south of Gaza.
Beloved, the eighth and youngest son of Jesse, a citizen of Bethlehem. His father seems to have been a man in humble life.
ch.s: This chapter covers: Ziklag spoiled by the Amalekites (vv. 1–6); David overtakes the Amalekites (vv. 7–15); He recovers what had been lost (vv. 16–20); David's distribution of the spoil (vv. 21–31). People named: David, Abiathar, Ahinoam, Abigail, Nabal, Ahimelech. Places: Ziklag, Besor, Judah, Egypt, Philistines.
ch.mh: When we go abroad in the way of our duty, we may comfortably hope that God will take care of our families in our absence, but not otherwise.
q: Read verses 1–6 (Ziklag spoiled by the Amalekites). What is happening, and what stands out to you most?
In verses 7–15 (David overtakes the Amalekites), what do you learn about family and generations?
Verse 6 is one of the most cross-referenced verses in this chapter. Read it alongside Psalms 56:3–4. How do the two passages shed light on each other?
What does David’s part in this chapter teach you — as an example to follow or a warning to heed?
Where do you see the theme of salvation and redemption in this chapter, and how does it connect to the rest of 1 Samuel?
What is one specific way you can put this chapter into practice this week?
ch.aq: What God gives us, he designs we should do good with.
ch.a: Thank God for His deliverance, and share what He has done for you with one person.

The first king of Israel, the son of Kish, and of the tribe of Benjamin. (B.C, 1095-1055.) His character is in part illustrated by the fierce, wayward, fitful nature of the tribe and in part accounted for by the struggle between the old and new systems in which he found himself involved.
ch.s: This chapter covers: Saul's defeat and death (vv. 1–7); Saul's body rescued by the men of Jabesh-gilead (vv. 8–13). People named: Saul, Jabesh, Jonathan, Abinadab. Places: Philistines, Gilboa, Jordan, Ashtaroth.
ch.mh: We cannot judge of the spiritual or eternal state of any by the manner of their death; for in that, there is one event to the righteous and to the wicked.
q: Read verses 1–7 (Saul's defeat and death). What is happening, and what stands out to you most?
